---
title: "Command-line interface"
guide-section: "Export & quality"
---

The `excel-grapher` command-line tool validates series-binding sidecars against workbooks,
audits resolution for codegen, prints an internals coverage worklist, optionally
smoke-tests generated `compute_*` functions, and can write export modules to disk.
It complements the Python APIs documented in [Series bindings](series-bindings.qmd)
and the authoring loop in [Authoring series bindings](binding-authoring.qmd).

Run it from the project environment:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings audit --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings burndown --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings upsert --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings viz --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings undomained --help
uv run excel-grapher bindings candidates --help
```

When the package is installed, `excel-grapher` is also available as a console script.

## Command overview

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `bindings validate` | Load a sidecar, build the dependency graph, and validate bindings against the workbook |
| `bindings audit` | Resolve bindings the way codegen does and fail if resolution is not `ok=True` |
| `bindings burndown` | Print unbound formula cells in the current bound graph closure as a coverage worklist (not a full workbook walk; not candidate bindings) |
| `bindings upsert` | Insert or replace one series after fail-closed schema, occupancy, and resolution checks |
| `bindings viz` | Write a statement-graph HTML visualization from series bindings |
| `bindings undomained` | Print graph leaves that have no bindings domain |
| `bindings candidates` | Print dynamic-ref leaves that still need a domain, before extract |

More subcommands may be added over time; `excel-grapher --help` lists what is available in your
installed version.

## `bindings validate`

Validate a workbook and its binding sidecar before export or CI.

### Synopsis

```bash
excel-grapher bindings validate WORKBOOK [--bindings PATH] [--json] [-v]
  [--smoke-test] [--emit-dir DIR] [--package-name NAME]
  [--use-cached-dynamic-refs] [--blank-ranges PATH]
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `WORKBOOK` | Path to the `.xlsx` workbook (required). |
| `--bindings PATH` | Binding sidecar **file** or **shard directory**. When omitted, the CLI looks for a colocated sidecar (see below). |
| `--json` | Print the full validation `report` object as JSON (includes every issue). |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Print **warnings** in human-readable output. **Errors** are always printed when validation fails. |
| `--smoke-test` | After a successful validation, generate binding modules and run `compute_*` smoke checks with workbook-default inputs. |
| `--emit-dir DIR` | Write generated module files under `DIR` (see `--package-name`). Implied when combined with `--smoke-test` and an emit directory. |
| `--package-name NAME` | Package directory name for smoke tests and emitted files (default: `bindings_module`). |
| `--use-cached-dynamic-refs` | Resolve those dynamic refs from the workbook's cached values instead of series domain. |
| `--blank-ranges PATH` | Optional Python module exposing `BLANK_RANGES: Sequence[str]` (sheet-qualified rectangles omitted from the graph). |

Validation-only is the default: no code is generated unless you pass `--smoke-test` or `--emit-dir`.

### Resolving the sidecar

When `--bindings` is omitted, `bindings validate` tries, in order:

1. `{workbook_stem}.bindings.yaml` next to the workbook
2. `{workbook_stem}.bindings/` (directory of `*.bindings.yaml` shards)

Pass `--bindings` explicitly when the sidecar lives elsewhere—for example a shared fixture:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate examples/micro_workbooks/ffv2.xlsx \
  --bindings tests/fixtures/series_bindings/ffv2.yaml
```

### Example: ffv2 game log

The [ffv2](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/excel-grapher/blob/main/examples/micro_workbooks/ffv2.xlsx)
micro-workbook uses datetime column headers as `TIME_PERIOD` keys. It is a **bindings
validation** demo: the published output rows are typed-in values, not formulas, so do not
pass `--smoke-test` or `--emit-dir` (those need a formula output series; see tiny-DSA below).
With a valid sidecar:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate examples/micro_workbooks/ffv2.xlsx \
  --bindings tests/fixtures/series_bindings/ffv2.yaml
```

Successful validation prints a short summary on stdout:

```text
ok=True errors=0 warnings=0
canonical_sha256=…
inputs=['puka_longest_reception', 'puka_receptions', …]
computes=['compute_puka_avg_yards_per_reception', …]
```

Add `-v` to include warnings (for example `dtype_read_mismatch` when a bind `read` mode disagrees
with a concept `dtype`):

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate examples/micro_workbooks/ffv2.xlsx \
  --bindings tests/fixtures/series_bindings/ffv2.yaml -v
```

Use `--json` for machine-readable output (the same structure returned by
`validate_series_bindings()`):

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate examples/micro_workbooks/ffv2.xlsx \
  --bindings tests/fixtures/series_bindings/ffv2.yaml --json
```

Each issue in the JSON report has `level`, `code`, `message`, and optional `series_id` and
`address` fields.

### Smoke test and code generation

After validation succeeds, `--smoke-test` generates an inverted-tree package, calls each
`compute_*` with the workbook-default tensors and scalars from `data.py`, and checks
the declared output coordinates and value contract. Export requires at least one formula output series.

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate lic_inputs.xlsx --smoke-test
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate lic_inputs.xlsx \
  --smoke-test --emit-dir ./generated
```

Workbooks that contain `OFFSET` / `INDEX` / `INDIRECT` with non-literal arguments need an
explicit resolution strategy. The sidecar's series `domain` (and `constant` pins)
is that strategy:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate \
  tests/fixtures/inverted_tree/tiny_dsa/tiny-dsa.xlsx \
  --bindings tests/fixtures/inverted_tree/tiny_dsa/bindings \
  --smoke-test
```

Without a bindings domain covering the `OFFSET` / `INDEX` / `INDIRECT` leaves,
and without `--use-cached-dynamic-refs`, graph building fails
with a message that names the cell and the flag to pass.

To persist generated files:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate lic_inputs.xlsx \
  --smoke-test --emit-dir ./generated --package-name lic_bindings
```

Without `--smoke-test`, `--emit-dir` alone writes modules after validation:

```bash
uv run excel-grapher bindings validate lic_inputs.xlsx --emit-dir ./generated
```

When smoke checks pass, the CLI prints:

```text
All compute functions passed smoke checks.
```

### Error output

Failures fall into two layers:

**Sidecar schema errors** — the YAML/JSON manifest does not satisfy the JSON Schema (missing
required fields, unknown properties, and so on). These are reported on **stderr** before workbook
validation runs:

```text
Binding sidecar schema error:
  series[8] "puka_week_1_fantasy_score": missing required field `key` — Add a key list naming the dimension ids that identify each record.
```

Locations use the series index and `id` from the sidecar so you can jump straight to the offending
entry.

**Workbook validation errors** — the sidecar parses, but coordinate resolution or binding rules
fail against the live workbook. These appear as human-readable lines on **stdout** (or inside
`issues[]` with `--json`):

```text
error [bind_resolution_failed] puka_targets:Sheet1!A4: could not convert string to float: 'Tgts'
```

When the same root cause affects many cells (for example a `read: float` bind over a row that
includes a text label), identical messages are **aggregated** into one issue with a cell count and
range rather than one line per cell.

Warnings such as `dtype_read_mismatch` do not fail validation by themselves; use `-v` to see them in
text mode.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Validation succeeded (and smoke tests passed, if requested). |
| `1` | Workbook or sidecar not found, schema error, validation failure, or smoke-test failure. |
| `2` | Unknown subcommand or invalid CLI usage. |

### Related Python APIs

The CLI wraps the same workflow as:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from excel_grapher.grapher.dynamic_refs import DynamicRefConfig
from excel_grapher.series_bindings import (
    load_series_bindings,
    validate_bindings_workbook,
    run_binding_checks,
)

workbook = Path("lic_inputs.xlsx")
bindings_path = workbook.with_suffix(".bindings.yaml")
bindings = load_series_bindings(bindings_path)
dynamic_refs = DynamicRefConfig.from_bindings(bindings, workbook, bindings_path=bindings_path)

result = validate_bindings_workbook(
    workbook,
    bindings_path,
    dynamic_refs=dynamic_refs,
    use_cached_dynamic_refs=False,
)
assert result["report"]["ok"]

run_binding_checks(
    workbook,
    bindings_path,
    module_dir=Path("./generated/lic_bindings"),
    package_name="lic_bindings",
    smoke_test=True,
    dynamic_refs=dynamic_refs,
    use_cached_dynamic_refs=False,
)
```

See [Series bindings](series-bindings.qmd) for manifest authoring, bind kinds, and export
integration, [Authoring series bindings](binding-authoring.qmd) for the agent skill and
audit/burndown loop, and [Exporting standalone Python](06-export.qmd) for inverted-tree
packages and the ctx migration.

## `bindings audit`

Resolve input, output, internal, and constant series the same way codegen does.
`bindings validate` does not require resolution `ok=True`; this command does.

```bash
excel-grapher bindings audit WORKBOOK [--bindings PATH] [--json]
  [--direction DIRECTION] [--strict]
  [--use-cached-dynamic-refs] [--blank-ranges PATH]
```

Exit `1` on error findings. `--strict` also fails on warnings such as
`empty_public_series`. Repeat `--direction` to limit the scan
(`input` / `output` / `internal` / `constant`).

## `bindings burndown`

Print formula nodes **in the current bound graph closure** (the graph built
from bound `data_range` targets) that are not covered by input, output, or
internal bindings as a **coverage worklist**. This is not a full workbook
walk; empty shards yield an empty graph. Collapsed A1 rectangles include a
weak layout hint (`scalar`, `series`, or `matrix`). Do not treat each printed
range as a series to emit.

```bash
excel-grapher bindings burndown WORKBOOK [--bindings PATH] [--json]
  [--per-sheet SHEET] [--max-rows N] [--exempt FILE] [--strict]
  [--use-cached-dynamic-refs] [--blank-ranges PATH]
```

`--exempt` is a text file of reviewed addresses (one per line; `#` comments
allowed). `--strict` exits `1` when unbound cells remain. `--max-rows` limits
row detail and prints `... (truncated)` when it cuts off.

## `bindings upsert`

Insert or replace **one** series after schema, occupancy, shard, and resolution
checks against a temporary copy. The destination is written only when those
checks succeed. There is no catalog → four-file bulk emitter.

```bash
excel-grapher bindings upsert WORKBOOK --series SERIES.yaml
  [--bindings PATH] [--replace]
  [--use-cached-dynamic-refs] [--blank-ranges PATH]
```

`SERIES.yaml` is one series mapping, or a document with `series: [one entry]`.
`--replace` updates an existing id. When `--bindings` is omitted and no
colocated sidecar exists, a successful upsert creates `{stem}.bindings/` with
four-file shards. A failed upsert leaves the destination unchanged.
`--use-cached-dynamic-refs` defaults to off on the CLI (same as `validate`);
the Python helper `upsert_series_binding` defaults it to on.

## `bindings undomained`

Print graph leaves that have no bindings `domain` / `from_workbook` coverage.
This is a domain-completeness worklist, distinct from `bindings burndown`
(unbound formula cells in the bound closure).

```bash
excel-grapher bindings undomained WORKBOOK [--bindings PATH] [--json]
  [--use-cached-dynamic-refs]
```

When every leaf is covered, the command prints
`ok: every graph leaf has a bindings domain`.

## `bindings candidates`

Print the pre-extract worklist: leaf addresses that feed `OFFSET` / `INDEX` /
`INDIRECT` and have no bindings domain yet. This does **not** build the
dependency graph and does **not** accept `--use-cached-dynamic-refs`.

```bash
excel-grapher bindings candidates WORKBOOK [--bindings PATH]
  [--target ADDR] [--json] [--strict] [--undomained-match]
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `WORKBOOK` | Path to the `.xlsx` workbook (required). |
| `--bindings PATH` | Sidecar file or shard directory. When omitted, the CLI looks for a colocated sidecar. |
| `--target ADDR` | Extraction root (sheet-qualified address, range, or defined name). Repeatable. Unioned with every series `data_range`. |
| `--json` | Print the address list as JSON. With `--undomained-match`, print `{"missing", "undomained_exact_match"}`. |
| `--strict` | Exit 1 while any must-bind candidate remains. Undomained MATCH cells do not fail `--strict`. |
| `--undomained-match` | Also print lookup cells exact MATCH kept only because they have no domain. Not merged into the must-bind list. |

Empty shards have no roots. Author an output series first, or pass `--target`
before a sidecar exists. The command prints one A1 address per line, or
`ok: no dynamic-ref leaves are missing a bindings domain`.

The list is incomplete until controlling domains are wide enough to reach the
next dynamic ref. Re-run after every domain edit on a dynamic-ref argument.
`INDEX`/`MATCH` over a static rectangle is often typed from range geometry and
does not appear on the must-bind list. When exact MATCH keeps a lookup cell
only because it has no domain, inference emits `ExactMatchUndomainedCellWarning`
and still succeeds. The warning lists cells the scan classified before a
certain hit. A scan with no certain hit prints a prefix and the total count.
An unpinned needle is not scanned and does not warn. `--undomained-match`
returns that same collection separately; it does not list proven misses or
cells after the hit. Defined names are resolved to addresses. `BLANK_RANGES` is
not applied; subtract those cells yourself. A blank cell pinned only with
`constant` stays on the list. A `greater_than` / `not_equal` whose partner
series is missing fails with `SeriesRelationError` before any list is printed.

Walked end to end (bindings domains only, no Python constraint table, no
cached dynamic refs) in
`tests/integration/grapher/test_extract_time_domain_loop.py`: a micro
workbook whose `OFFSET` uses a defined name and whose row domain must be
widened before the downstream `INDIRECT` appears, then tiny-DSA output roots,
which need only `Inputs!B22` (`shock_type`) before extract. Remaining leaves
are an `undomained` / `attach_domains` pass, not a second extract.
Q-CRAFT `Macrofiscal!C3` (`INDEX`/`MATCH` on a static country column) and
`Discrete Risks!C2:BT13` return an empty candidate list for the same reason:
those selectors do not need a leaf domain.
